Title: Create a league
User story: As a league admin, I want to set up a new league with its season dates, format and points system, so that everything is configured before teams start registering.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject empty or whitespace-only league name. 2) Reject a name already used by another league. 3) Reject team count below 4. 4) Reject team count above 24. 5) Reject season end date on or before start date. 6) Reject a season shorter than the minimum weeks needed for the format. 7) Format must be 'single' or 'double' round-robin, else reject. 8) Points for a win must be greater than points for a draw, else reject. 9) Points for a loss must be 0 or less than points for a draw, else reject. 10) Return a list of all validation errors rather than stopping at the first.
Estimate notes: Planning Poker result was 8. Re-estimated to 13 by team agreement on 26 Nov 2026 to balance workload; not re-voted in Planning Poker.

Title: Register a team
User story: As a league admin, I want to add a team to the league with its name, short code and home ground, so that only valid teams with unique names end up in the competition.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the league does not exist. 2) Reject if fixtures have already been generated (registration closed). 3) Reject if the league is already full. 4) Reject a duplicate team name (case-insensitive). 5) Short code must be exactly 3 letters, else reject. 6) Reject a duplicate short code. 7) Reject if no home stadium is given. 8) Reject if stadium capacity is below the league minimum. 9) Flag (warn, not reject) if the team's stadium is already used by another team.
Estimate notes: Planning Poker result was 5. Re-estimated to 8 by team agreement on 26 Nov 2026 to balance workload; not re-voted in Planning Poker.

Title: Assign a stadium (including ground shares)
User story: As a league admin, I want to give each team a home stadium and allow two teams to share one, so that we never end up with two home games at the same ground on the same day.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the stadium does not exist. 2) Reject if the team does not exist. 3) Allow immediately if the stadium has no current tenant. 4) Reject if the stadium already has 2 tenants (max ground share). 5) Reject if the tenant team is withdrawn (ground share must be with an active team). 6) Reject if capacity is below the league minimum. 7) Reject if the stadium's unavailable dates cover more than 25% of the season. 8) Mark both teams as ground-share partners when a second tenant is added. 9) Reject re-assigning a team to the stadium it already uses. 10) If the team had a previous stadium, release it and update that stadium's tenant list. 11) Block the change after fixtures are generated unless forced by an administrator.

Title: Check a squad against registration rules
User story: As a team manager, I want my squad checked against the league's registration rules (squad size, goalkeepers, loans, shirt numbers), so that I know before the season whether my team is eligible.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject fewer than 18 registered players. 2) Reject more than 25 registered players. 3) Reject fewer than 2 goalkeepers. 4) Reject more than 5 loan players. 5) Reject duplicate shirt numbers. 6) Reject shirt numbers outside 1-99. 7) Reject any player under 16. 8) Reject a player registered to another team in the same league. 9) After the registration deadline, only allow changes during the transfer window. 10) Return each failing rule with the player it applies to.

Title: Change a team's status
User story: As a league admin, I want to move a team between active, suspended and withdrawn, so that disciplinary decisions are recorded properly and the affected fixtures are easy to find.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown status value. 2) Reject a change to the same status. 3) Active → suspended allowed only with a reason. 4) Suspension must have an end date after today. 5) Suspended → active allowed only on or after the suspension end date, unless overridden. 6) Active or suspended → withdrawn requires administrator confirmation. 7) Withdrawn is final: reject any change away from withdrawn. 8) Before the season starts, withdrawing removes the team instead of marking it. 9) Log every status change with date and reason. 10) Return the list of future fixtures affected by the change.
Estimate notes: Planning Poker result was 5. Re-estimated to 8 by team agreement on 26 Nov 2026 to balance workload; not re-voted in Planning Poker.

Title: Readiness check before generating fixtures
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want a readiness report on the league before I generate fixtures, so that the generator never runs on missing stadiums, bad squads or impossible dates.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Fail if the league has fewer than 4 active teams. 2) Warn if the team count is odd (a bye will be needed). 3) Fail if any active team has no stadium. 4) Fail if any team's squad is invalid (uses Jose-4). 5) Fail if fixtures already exist. 6) Fail if season dates are missing or invalid. 7) Fail if the number of available weekends is less than the number of rounds. 8) Warn if there are ground-share pairs (constraint for Yousef-2). 9) Warn if no derby pairs are defined. 10) Warn if any stadium has unavailable dates inside the season. 11) Return status READY, READY_WITH_WARNINGS or NOT_READY with all messages.

Title: Team withdraws mid-season
User story: As a league admin, I want to handle a team pulling out during the season (expunging or awarding its matches depending on how far in we are), so that the table stays fair for everyone else.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the team is already withdrawn. 2) Reject if the season has finished. 3) If the season has not started, remove the team and flag fixtures for regeneration. 4) If fewer than half of the team's matches are played, expunge all its results. 5) If half or more are played, keep played results. 6) Then award remaining matches to opponents using the league's forfeit score. 7) Cancel all future fixtures involving the team. 8) Free any ground-share partner's stadium constraints. 9) If withdrawal leaves fewer than 4 active teams, mark the league as void. 10) Request a standings recalculation (uses Ismail-2). 11) Record the withdrawal reason and date. 12) Return a summary of expunged, awarded and cancelled matches.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.29 (postponements/forfeits); EFL Trophy rule 20 (forfeit awards)
Estimate notes: Planning Poker result was 8. Re-estimated to 13 by team agreement on 26 Nov 2026 to balance workload; not re-voted in Planning Poker.

Title: Edit league settings once the season is set up
User story: As a league admin, I want to change league settings, but with some of them locked once fixtures or results exist, so that a late change can't break the schedule or the table.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown setting name. 2) Name change allowed at any time but must stay unique. 3) Team count change blocked once fixtures exist. 4) Format change blocked once fixtures exist. 5) Points system change blocked once the first result is recorded. 6) Start date change blocked once the season has started. 7) End date can be extended but not moved before the last scheduled fixture. 8) Zone sizes (promotion/relegation) cannot exceed half the team count. 9) Zone size change blocked in the final 5 rounds. 10) Every accepted change is logged with old and new value.

Title: Save and load the league from a file
User story: As a league admin, I want the league saved to and loaded from a JSON file with clear error messages, so that nothing is lost between sessions and a corrupt file doesn't wipe our data.
Acceptance criteria: 1) File not found → clear error. 2) Empty file → clear error. 3) Invalid JSON → clear error. 4) Missing required top-level section → name the section. 5) File version newer than supported → reject. 6) File version older → migrate known fields. 7) Duplicate team IDs in file → reject. 8) Fixture referencing an unknown team → reject. 9) Result recorded for a fixture that does not exist → reject. 10) On save, write to a temporary file first and replace only on success. 11) On save failure, keep the previous file intact and report the error.
Estimate notes: Planning Poker result was 8. Re-estimated to 13 by team agreement on 26 Nov 2026 to balance workload; not re-voted in Planning Poker.

Title: Generate round-robin pairings
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want the system to pair every team against every other team (with a bye if the number is odd), so that the season has a complete set of matches.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject fewer than 2 teams. 2) Reject duplicate teams in the input. 3) Ignore withdrawn teams. 4) If the team count is odd, add a BYE placeholder. 5) Use the circle method: fix one team, rotate the others each round. 6) Skip any pairing involving BYE when building matches (record the bye instead). 7) Single format → n-1 rounds. 8) Double format → 2(n-1) rounds (second half produced by Yousef-3). 9) Reject an unknown format value.
Research source: Rasmussen & Trick, Round robin scheduling - a survey (circle method)

Title: Balance home and away games
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want home and away games spread evenly for each team, with no more than two in a row at home or away, so that no club gets a lopsided run.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Alternate home/away for each team where possible. 2) A 'break' is two consecutive home or two consecutive away games. 3) Reject any assignment creating 3 consecutive home games. 4) Reject any assignment creating 3 consecutive away games. 5) Ground-share partners must not both be at home in the same round. 6) A team's first and last match must not both be away. 7) A team's first two matches must not both be home or both be away. 8) A team with a bye keeps its home/away pattern after the bye. 9) If no valid assignment exists for a round, flip the fixed team's venue and retry once. 10) If still invalid, report the round and team that could not be satisfied. 11) Return the number of breaks per team.
Research source: van 't Hof et al. 2010, fair round robins with a minimum number of breaks

Title: Mirror the second half of the season
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want the second half of a double round-robin to reverse the home and away teams from the first half, so that every team hosts every opponent once.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if format is single (no second half). 2) Reject if the first half is incomplete. 3) Reverse home/away for every first-half match. 4) Keep byes in the same relative round. 5) If mirroring creates 3 consecutive home or away games, swap with the next round. 6) If mirroring makes ground-share partners both at home, swap with the next round. 7) If no swap fixes it, report the conflict. 8) The same pair must not meet in the last round of the first half and the first round of the second half. 9) Check each pair meets exactly twice, once at each ground.

Title: Put dates on each round
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want each round given a date, mainly Saturdays, skipping international breaks and adding midweek rounds if the calendar is tight, so that the whole season fits between the start and end dates.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if season dates are missing. 2) Default to Saturdays. 3) Skip blackout dates (international breaks, Christmas Day). 4) If a Saturday is a blackout, try the Sunday of the same weekend. 5) If there aren't enough weekends, insert midweek (Tuesday) rounds. 6) A midweek round must be at least 3 days from the weekend rounds either side. 7) No more than 2 midweek rounds in any 4-week period. 8) If rounds still don't fit, fail with the number of missing dates. 9) The last round of the season is always on a weekend. 10) If any team's stadium is unavailable on the round date, flag it for Anay-1. 11) Return the date for every round.

Title: Spread out the derbies
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want derby matches kept off the first and last rounds and spaced apart, so that rivalry games aren't bunched together.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Skip if no derby pairs are defined. 2) Reject a derby pair containing an unknown team. 3) A derby must not be in round 1. 4) A derby must not be in the final round. 5) The two legs of a derby must be at least N rounds apart (configurable, default 6). 6) A team must not play derbies in consecutive rounds. 7) No more than 2 derbies in the same round. 8) Fix a violation by swapping whole rounds, never individual matches. 9) Re-check home/away break rules after any swap. 10) Report derbies that could not be placed.

Title: Set kick-off times
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want a kick-off time set for each match using the default slots, TV picks and the police rule on evening derbies, so that every fixture has a time that's actually allowed.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Saturday default is 15:00. 2) Sunday default is 14:00. 3) Midweek default is 19:45. 4) Derbies cannot kick off after 18:00 (police safety rule). 5) High-capacity stadiums (over 30,000) cannot host evening derbies. 6) Matches picked for TV move to the broadcaster slot (uses Anay-3). 7) A team cannot have a Sunday game followed by a Tuesday evening game. 8) Ground-share stadiums cannot host two matches on the same day. 9) Matches in the final round all kick off at the same time. 10) Reject a manually supplied time outside 12:00-20:00.

Title: Validate the fixture list
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want the full fixture list checked for mistakes (a team playing twice in a round, wrong number of meetings, clashing venues), so that we never publish a broken schedule.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Fail if any pair meets the wrong number of times for the format. 2) Fail if a team appears twice in the same round. 3) Fail if a team plays itself. 4) Fail if home/away counts per team differ by more than 1. 5) Fail if any team has 3 consecutive home or away games. 6) Fail if a round has no date. 7) Fail if the same stadium hosts two matches on one date. 8) Warn if a team has more than one bye. 9) Warn if derby spacing rules are broken. 10) Warn if any match is outside the season dates. 11) Return VALID, VALID_WITH_WARNINGS or INVALID with all messages.

Title: Regenerate fixtures after a pre-season change
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want to rebuild the fixtures if a team joins or drops out before the season starts, so that the schedule always matches who is actually in the league.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the season has started. 2) Reject if no team change happened since the last generation. 3) If a team was added and the count becomes odd, add a bye. 4) If a team was removed and the count becomes even, remove the bye. 5) Keep existing round dates where the round count is unchanged. 6) If the round count changes, re-run date assignment (Yousef-4). 7) Keep derby pairs that are still valid, drop pairs with removed teams. 8) Re-run validation (Yousef-7). 9) If validation fails, restore the previous fixture list. 10) Log the regeneration with the reason.

Title: Search and filter fixtures
User story: As a supporter, I want to filter fixtures by team, round, date range and home or away, so that I can find the games I care about without scrolling through the whole list.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown team name. 2) Reject a round number outside 1..total rounds. 3) Reject a date range where start is after end. 4) Reject a venue filter other than home/away/any. 5) Venue filter without a team → reject (home/away needs a team). 6) Apply each filter only if it was supplied. 7) Exclude postponed matches unless include_postponed is set. 8) Sort by date, then kick-off time, then home team. 9) Return an empty list (not an error) when nothing matches. 10) Limit results to 50 and report if truncated.

Title: Check a venue for clashes
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want to know if a stadium is already booked or unavailable on a given date, so that a ground is never double-booked.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match or stadium does not exist. 2) Clash if the same stadium hosts another match that day. 3) Clash if the stadium is marked unavailable that day. 4) Clash if a ground-share partner is at home that day. 5) For ground shares, allow back-to-back days only if at least 24 hours apart. 6) Ignore postponed or cancelled matches when checking. 7) Ignore the match being checked (rescheduling the same match). 8) Warn (not clash) for a non-football event within 24 hours. 9) Return NO_CLASH, WARNING or CLASH with the conflicting item. 10) Check all stadium rules before returning, so every conflict is listed.

Title: Check rest days between matches
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want to check that both teams get at least 48 hours between games (more after an evening kick-off), so that players get fair recovery time.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if either team does not exist. 2) Find each team's nearest match before and after the proposed date. 3) Fail if any gap is under 48 hours. 4) Fail if the gap is under 72 hours after an evening (19:45) kick-off. 5) Warn if the gap is under 72 hours otherwise. 6) Fail if a team has a cup match within 48 hours. 7) Ignore postponed or cancelled matches. 8) Check both teams and report each team separately. 9) If no previous or next match exists, treat that side as OK.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.27 (48-hour recovery between fixtures)

Title: Check TV slot rules
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want a TV pick checked against the broadcast rules, including the Saturday 2:45 to 5:15pm blackout and the notice period, so that moves for TV follow league regulations.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match does not exist. 2) Reject a TV slot between 14:45 and 17:15 on a Saturday (UK blackout). 3) Reject a pick made with less than 5 weeks' notice, unless both clubs agree. 4) Reject if two TV matches share the same slot. 5) Reject if a team exceeds its maximum TV picks per season. 6) Warn if a team falls below its minimum TV picks with less than 10 rounds left. 7) Moving to a Sunday must still meet rest rules (uses Anay-2). 8) Moving to a Friday is blocked for a team that played on the Tuesday before. 9) Final-round matches cannot be moved for TV. 10) Return ALLOWED, ALLOWED_WITH_WARNING or REJECTED with the reason. 11) Record the original slot so the move can be undone.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.27 (selections usually 5 weeks' notice; Saturday 14:45-17:15 restriction)

Title: Postpone a match
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want to postpone a match and record why (weather, pitch, cup, international duty and so on), so that games that can't go ahead are handled formally rather than just disappearing.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match does not exist. 2) Reject if the match is already played. 3) Reject if the match is already postponed. 4) Reject if the match is in progress. 5) Reason must be one of weather, pitch, cup, international, safety, other. 6) Reason 'other' requires a free-text explanation. 7) Cup or international postponements require at least 7 days' notice. 8) A club cannot postpone its own match: the request must come from the league administrator. 9) If a team already has 3 or more postponed matches, flag for review. 10) Set status to POSTPONED and record reason and date.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.29 (club cannot postpone; League decides)

Title: Find the next free date for a postponed match
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want the system to suggest the earliest date that works for both teams and the venue, so that postponed games get rearranged quickly.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match is not postponed. 2) Search from tomorrow up to the rearrangement deadline. 3) Skip blackout dates. 4) Skip dates where either team plays (uses Anay-2). 5) Skip dates with a venue clash (uses Anay-1). 6) Prefer midweek dates over weekends. 7) Skip dates that would give either team 3 consecutive home or away games. 8) Skip dates after the second-last round (all postponed matches must finish before the final round). 9) If the deadline is reached, report that no date is available. 10) If both clubs proposed a preferred date and it is valid, return that first. 11) Return the chosen date and how many candidates were rejected, and why. 12) Report the number of days of notice the date gives.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.29 (re-dating considers home/away either side, cup clashes)

Title: Reschedule a match
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want to move a match to a new date, with checks for notice periods and the clubs' agreement, so that every rearrangement follows the rules.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match is played or cancelled. 2) Reject if the new date is the same as the current one. 3) Reject a new date after the season end. 4) Reject a new date with a venue clash (Anay-1). 5) Reject a new date that breaks rest rules (Anay-2). 6) Tuesday match with under 28 days' notice: allow only a 24-hour move to Wednesday. 7) A move of more than 14 days requires both clubs' agreement. 8) A move into the final round requires administrator override. 9) Notify both clubs; if less than 7 days' notice, flag as SHORT_NOTICE. 10) Update status from POSTPONED to SCHEDULED if it was postponed. 11) Record the old date in the match history.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.27.4 (Tuesday->Wednesday 24-hour postponement, 28 clear days)

Title: Warn about fixture congestion
User story: As a team manager, I want a warning when my team has too many games packed into a short period, so that we can ask for a rearrangement early.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown team. 2) Reject a window of 0 days or less. 3) Count matches (league + cup) inside the rolling window. 4) OK if the count is at or under the limit. 5) WARNING if the count is 1 over the limit. 6) CRITICAL if the count is 2 or more over the limit. 7) Count postponed matches only if they already have a new date. 8) Escalate one level if the window includes 2 away games over 200 miles (travel). 9) Escalate one level if the window ends in the final 3 rounds. 10) Return the worst window found and its dates.

Title: Sort out cup clashes
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want league games moved automatically when a team reaches a cup round on the same date, so that cup runs don't cause double-bookings.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the cup date is outside the season. 2) No clash if neither team in the league match is in the cup that day. 3) If one team is in the cup, postpone the league match (Anay-4, reason 'cup'). 4) If both teams are in the cup, postpone and mark as high priority to rearrange. 5) A cup replay creates a clash on the replay date as well. 6) A cup final weekend postpones every league match involving the finalists. 7) If the team is knocked out, cancel provisional postponements for later rounds. 8) A postponed match created here goes straight into Anay-5 for a new date. 9) If no new date exists, flag for administrator decision. 10) Record the link between the cup round and the postponed league match. 11) Report all league matches affected.
Research source: EFL Regulations s.29.2 and s.31 (cup clashes and FA Cup re-arrangement)

Title: Decide what happens to an abandoned match
User story: As a league admin, I want the outcome of an abandoned match decided by the cause (weather, crowd trouble, one or both teams' conduct), so that abandonments are treated the same way every time.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match was not in progress. 2) Reject an unknown abandonment cause. 3) Cause outside both clubs' control (weather, floodlights): replay in full. 4) Exception: if 80 or more minutes were played, the league can let the result stand. 5) Caused by conduct of the home team or its supporters: award match to away team. 6) Caused by conduct of the away team or its supporters: award match to home team. 7) Caused by conduct of both teams: no points for either side, no replay. 8) Awarded matches use the league forfeit score, or the actual score if the winner was leading by more. 9) A replay is sent to Anay-5 to find a date. 10) Points are not counted until the decision is confirmed. 11) Record the minute of abandonment and the decision.
Research source: FA match abandonment rules (Rule 20(E)); EFL Trophy rule 20.6

Title: Record a match result
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want to enter the final score of a match, so that the league table is built from accurate results.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the match does not exist. 2) Reject a negative score. 3) Reject a score over 30 (likely data entry error). 4) Reject a result for a match dated in the future. 5) Reject a result for a postponed or cancelled match. 6) Reject a result for an abandoned match awaiting decision. 7) If a result already exists, reject unless 'override' is set. 8) An override requires a reason and is logged. 9) Set status to PLAYED. 10) Trigger a team record update (Ismail-2).

Title: Update team records after a result
User story: As the fixture secretary, I want each team's played, won, drawn, lost, goals and points updated when a result goes in (forfeits included), so that the table always matches the results.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if the result's teams are not in the league. 2) Home win: home gets win points, away gets loss points. 3) Away win: away gets win points, home gets loss points. 4) Draw: both get draw points. 5) Forfeit: winner gets the forfeit score and win points, loser gets loss points. 6) Both teams forfeit: both get 0 points and a loss. 7) Result of an expunged team: ignore it. 8) Override of a previous result: reverse the old result first. 9) Update goals for, goals against and goal difference. 10) Update the home/away split counters.
Research source: EFL Trophy rule 20 (forfeit awards); FA Rule 20(E) (no points where both teams at fault)

Title: Compare two teams with the tie-breakers
User story: As a supporter, I want teams on the same points separated by goal difference, then goals scored, then head-to-head, so that league positions are decided the way the Premier League does it.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Higher points ranks first. 2) If points are equal, higher goal difference ranks first. 3) If still equal, more goals scored ranks first. 4) If still equal, more head-to-head points ranks first. 5) If still equal, more away goals in head-to-head matches ranks first. 6) If still equal and the position decides the title, promotion or relegation, flag a play-off. 7) Otherwise order alphabetically. 8) Withdrawn teams are always ranked last. 9) A team with expunged results compares on its remaining results. 10) If head-to-head matches are not all played, skip the head-to-head criteria. 11) Return -1, 0 or 1 (for use as a sort comparator).
Research source: Premier League tie-break order: points, GD, goals scored, head-to-head points, head-to-head away goals, play-off

Title: Head-to-head mini-table for tied teams
User story: As a supporter, I want a mini-table of the games between teams that are still level, so that ties between three or more teams are broken fairly.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject fewer than 2 teams. 2) Only include matches where both teams are in the tied group. 3) Ignore unplayed, postponed and abandoned-without-result matches. 4) If any match in the group is unplayed, mark the mini-table as provisional. 5) Score each match with league points (win/draw/loss). 6) Count away goals separately. 7) If one team is separated, remove it and re-apply to the remaining tied teams. 8) If no team separates, fall back to play-off flag or alphabetical (as Ismail-3). 9) A 2-team tie uses the same logic (no special case). 10) Return the ordered group and the criterion that decided each place. 11) A forfeited match counts with its awarded score.
Research source: Premier League tie-break rules (head-to-head points then head-to-head away goals)

Title: Apply or reverse a points deduction
User story: As a league admin, I want to deduct points from a team (and reverse it if an appeal succeeds), so that sanctions show up correctly in the table.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown team. 2) Reject a deduction of 0. 3) Reject a deduction greater than 30. 4) A reason is required. 5) Allow a deduction before the season starts (team starts negative). 6) Allow the total to go negative. 7) Reject a deduction for a withdrawn team. 8) A suspended deduction is recorded but not applied until activated. 9) Reversing a deduction requires the original deduction ID. 10) Reject reversing an already reversed deduction. 11) Trigger a standings recalculation.

Title: Show promotion, play-off and relegation zones
User story: As a supporter, I want each place in the table labelled as promotion, play-off, safe or relegation, so that I can see what each team is playing for.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if zone sizes overlap or exceed the number of teams. 2) Positions 1..automatic promotion → PROMOTION. 3) Next play-off positions → PLAYOFF. 4) Bottom relegation positions → RELEGATION. 5) Everyone else → SAFE. 6) If promotion size is 0, the top position is CHAMPION only. 7) Withdrawn teams count as relegated and the relegation zone shrinks by one. 8) If the league is top division, promotion zones become 'qualification' zones. 9) A team with a points deduction can move zone: recalculated each time. 10) Return position, team and zone for every team.

Title: Show a team's form and streaks
User story: As a supporter, I want to see a team's last few results and its current winning, unbeaten or winless run, so that I can tell how they're playing at the moment.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown team. 2) Reject a form length outside 1-10 (default 5). 3) If no matches are played, return 'no form'. 4) If fewer matches than the form length, use all played matches and flag it. 5) Map each result to W, D or L from this team's point of view. 6) A forfeit win counts as W, a forfeit loss as L. 7) Track the current winning streak. 8) Track the current unbeaten streak (wins and draws). 9) Track the current winless streak. 10) Filter by home only, away only or all. 11) Flag 'in form' if 2.0 or more points per game over the window, 'poor form' if under 1.0.

Title: Season summary report
User story: As a league admin, I want a summary of the season (best attack, best defence, biggest win, longest unbeaten run), so that I can share the key stats with clubs.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject if no matches are played. 2) Mark the report as provisional if the season is not finished. 3) Best attack: most goals scored (ties listed together). 4) Best defence: fewest goals conceded (ties listed together). 5) Biggest win: largest margin, then most goals scored. 6) Highest-scoring match. 7) Longest unbeaten run (uses Ismail-7). 8) Exclude expunged results. 9) Include the number of postponed and abandoned matches. 10) Include total points deducted per team, if any. 11) Write the report to a text file; report an error if writing fails.

Title: Has the title or relegation been decided?
User story: As a supporter, I want to know when a team has mathematically won the league or been relegated, so that it can be confirmed as soon as nobody can catch them.
Acceptance criteria: 1) Reject an unknown team. 2) Max possible points = current points + games left × points for a win. 3) CHAMPION if the leader's points exceed every other team's maximum. 4) If the leader's points equal a rival's maximum, CHAMPION only if the rival can't overtake on goal difference this season. 5) Otherwise NOT_DECIDED for the title. 6) RELEGATED if the team's maximum is below the points of the team just above the relegation zone. 7) If the team's maximum equals that team's points, decide on goal difference as above. 8) SAFE if the team's points exceed the maximum of every team in the relegation zone. 9) Point deductions are included in current points. 10) Withdrawn teams are excluded. 11) If any matches are postponed with no date, still count them as games left. 12) Return status and the number of points needed to secure the outcome.
